label: .github/workflows/spec-kit-check.yml:3-8 triggers only on pull_request to main with paths .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/** and the workflow file; there is no push key, so on a direct push to main or skilled/v* (documented as a real flow by routing-registry-drift.yml:3-8 'release-line pushes land directly (no PR)') none of its lanes run: CLI check gate + typecheck (40-44), shared package tests (46-47), CLI vitest project (49-53), legacy module lanes + bash validation suites (55-61), runtime vitest project (63-69), mirror parity checks (86-93). The gate the round-one census recorded as closing the CI-invisibility gaps never fires on the repository's own direct-push flow.

.github/workflows/changed-packet-validation.yml:3-5 triggers only on pull_request branches [main] with no push key and no paths, so a direct push to main lands spec-packet changes without the packet-validation lane ever running, while sibling gates (command-tree-parity.yml, playbook-operator-contract.yml) do run on push main — the PR-only choice is not a rule of the repo.

Of 15 workflows under .github/workflows, 8 never run on any push (agent-mirror-sync, changed-packet-validation, comment-hygiene, markdown-link-integrity, prompt-card-sync, rule-canary-sync, skill-doc-frontmatter, spec-kit-check) while 7 do (advisory-checks, command-tree-parity, naming-standard-guard, playbook-operator-contract, routing-registry-drift, runtime-no-spec-import, plus schedule/dispatch-only strict-pass-freshness-report); only routing-registry-drift.yml:3-8 documents the direct-push reality, and no README classifies which gates are push-eligible or why.
